stem: After how many hours will the camera have 150 images stored?
stimulus: A telescope's camera already has 30 images of a star field stored. It adds 15 new images every hour.
explanation: Write starting amount + (rate)(time) = total: $30 + 15h = 150$. Subtract the starting 30 to get $15h = 120$, then divide by 15 to get $h = 8$. This start-plus-rate setup is the base of every SAT question that gives you a fixed starting amount and a steady rate and asks 'after how many hours' or 'how many months'. If you write and solve this equation without thinking, you can spend your time on the story in the real question.

A.why: You divided the starting 30 images by the rate of 15. That tells you how many hours' worth of images were already stored. It does not tell you how long it takes to reach 150.

C.why: You divided 150 by 15 without first subtracting the 30 images that were already stored. The starting amount has to come off the total before you divide by the rate.

D.why: You found $150 - 30 = 120$, which is the number of new images needed, and stopped there. The question asks for hours, so you still need to divide by 15.

stem: After how many more days will the musicologist have transcribed all 40 pages?
stimulus: A musicologist is transcribing a 40-page handwritten symphony score. She has already transcribed 12 pages, and she transcribes 4 pages each day.
explanation: Write starting amount + (rate)(days) = total: $12 + 4d = 40$. Subtract 12 to get $4d = 28$, then divide by 4 to get $d = 7$. This is the core step in SAT word problems where some of the work is already done and a steady rate finishes it. You take the starting amount off first, then divide by the rate.

B.why: You divided 40 by 4 without subtracting the 12 pages that were already done. That gives the days for the whole score from scratch, not the days still needed.

C.why: You added the 12 pages to 40 instead of subtracting them, which gave $52 \div 4 = 13$. To undo $+12$ you subtract 12 from both sides.

D.why: 28 is the number of pages left to transcribe, $40 - 12$. The question asks for days, so you still need to divide by 4 pages per day.

stem: After how many hours will 36 bags be left to sift?
stimulus: An archaeology crew starts the morning with 90 bags of excavated soil to sift for artifacts. The crew sifts 6 bags every hour.
explanation: The amount goes down, so write starting amount − (rate)(time) = what is left: $90 - 6h = 36$. Subtract 90 to get $-6h = -54$, then divide by $-6$ to get $h = 9$. The SAT also writes this setup the other way around, as a quantity that drops by a fixed amount each period and a question about when it reaches a certain level. The equation has the same shape with the sign of the rate flipped.

A.why: You divided the 36 remaining bags by 6. That gives how long it would take to sift the bags that are left. The question asks how long it takes to get down to 36.

C.why: You divided 90 by 6, which is the time to sift every bag until none are left. The target is 36 bags remaining, not 0.

D.why: 54 is the number of bags sifted, $90 - 36$. That is the amount removed, not the time. Divide by 6 bags per hour to get hours.

stem: How many test kits can the health department buy?
stimulus: A county health department has \$280 to spend on a screening event. It must pay a one-time \$120 equipment fee, and each test kit costs \$8. It spends the rest of the money on test kits.
explanation: Write fee + (price per kit)(number of kits) = total: $120 + 8n = 280$. Subtract the \$120 fee to get $8n = 160$, then divide by 8 to get $n = 20$ kits. This is the fee-plus-charge setup behind SAT questions about a sign-up fee plus a monthly cost or a fixed charge plus a per-item price. The one-time amount comes off before you divide.

B.why: You divided \$280 by \$8 and forgot to subtract the one-time \$120 fee first. That money is not available for test kits.

C.why: You added the \$120 fee to \$280 instead of subtracting it, which gave $400 \div 8 = 50$. The fee uses up part of the budget, so it comes off the total.

D.why: 160 is the number of dollars left for test kits, $280 - 120$. The question asks how many kits, so divide the dollars by \$8 per kit.
